disclaimer: Compiled from public reporting and vendor announcements. Valuations and funding are as last publicly reported and may be stale. 'Models' reflects publicly disclosed foundation-model use only; most vendors are multi-model and do not disclose routing. Fields left null are genuinely unknown, not zero.

categories.platform: Foundation-model vendor selling directly into legal
categories.assistant: Horizontal legal AI assistant / firm-wide platform
categories.research: Primary law, case law data and research
categories.infra: DMS, knowledge, firm operations and deal infrastructure
categories.practice_mgmt: Practice management for small and mid-size firms
categories.ai_native_firm: AI-native law firm or legal service provider (sells outcomes, not seats)
categories.buyer: Law firm or legal department building rather than buying

companies.name: Harvey
companies.last_round: $200M co-led by GIC and Sequoia, Mar 2026
companies.what_it_does: Firm-wide assistant for research, drafting, diligence and workflow automation, sold to large firms and enterprise legal departments.
companies.model_note: Originally OpenAI-exclusive (an OpenAI Startup Fund portfolio company from Dec 2022). Opened to Anthropic and Google models in May 2025; users can pick a model or let Harvey auto-route. Publishing its own model research (Tenet) and moving toward a proprietary legal model.

platform_integrations.anthropic: MCP connector in Claude for Legal
platform_integrations.openai: Astra for Law API customer + ChatGPT plugin

companies.traction: Reported 40+ Am Law 100 firms; publishes BigLaw Bench

companies.name: Legora
companies.last_round: $550M Series D at $5.55B (Mar 10 2026), extended +$50M in Apr 2026 with Atlassian and NVentures (NVIDIA)
companies.what_it_does: Collaborative legal AI platform. Best known for Tabular Review — turning a folder of contracts into an interactive grid for clause comparison and extraction at scale — plus agentic workflows spanning drafting, review, research and translation.
companies.model_note: Anthropic publishes Legora as a Claude customer, using Claude across assistant, document review and workflows. Also an OpenAI API customer with Astra for Law access.

platform_integrations.anthropic: Named Claude for Legal partner + published Claude customer
platform_integrations.openai: Astra for Law API customer + ChatGPT plugin

companies.traction: Aggressive US buildout: NY (11 Madison Ave, ~100k sq ft), Denver, Houston, Chicago; 300+ US staff targeted by end of 2026

companies.name: Thomson Reuters — CoCounsel Legal
companies.what_it_does: Agentic legal platform grounded in Westlaw primary law and Practical Law, taking a matter from research and issue analysis to work product in one workflow. Next generation reached GA 2026-08-20.
companies.model_note: Next-gen CoCounsel Legal is built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK — it plans, selects tools, retrieves authoritative content and adapts mid-workflow.

platform_integrations.anthropic: Built on Claude Agent SDK; CoCounsel MCP connector exposes Westlaw + Practical Law inside Claude

companies.traction: Distribution is the moat: bundled with Westlaw and Practical Law, already the default research stack in most large US firms

companies.name: LexisNexis — Lexis+ AI / Protégé
companies.what_it_does: Agentic legal assistant across research, analysis, drafting and review, preserving matter context between steps. Expanded agentic capabilities announced 2026-08-24, four days after CoCounsel's next-gen GA.
companies.model_note: Historically multi-model across Anthropic, OpenAI and Mistral; routing not publicly disclosed.
companies.traction: The other half of the research duopoly; competing head-on with CoCounsel for the layer where lawyers finish work

companies.name: Clio
companies.what_it_does: Practice management for small and mid-size firms — intake, matters, billing, payments — now with AI layered across. Acquired vLex (~$1B, 2025), buying its way into legal research.
companies.traction: Owns the long tail of the profession — the segment BigLaw-focused vendors don't serve

companies.what_it_does: Dominant e-discovery platform (RelativityOne), with aiR for Review and related generative layers.

platform_integrations.anthropic: MCP connector in Claude for Legal

companies.traction: Incumbent with the corpus — review data is the asset everyone else lacks
